subject: Request: segmented forensic retention criteria & collection playbook
messages:
From: Alex Burns <alex.burns@medforge.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.com
Cc: security-ops@medforge.com
Date: Sun, 5 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: segmented forensic retention criteria & collection playbook

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team needs two things to close our SIG/AICPA review: a clear, customer-specific justification for retaining request/trace logs beyond your standard 90-day TTL for our account, and a short playbook describing how Redwood would collect and export forensic artifacts if we request a targeted investigation (tenant filters, time ranges, hashes, export format).

MedForge has an active incident response process and for regulatory reasons we may ask for up to 18 months of request metadata in a small number of cases (controlled exceptions). Can you provide:
- A description of the conditional criteria Redwood uses to approve longer-than-default retention for a customer (who signs off, evidence required).
- The technical retention buckets you can support (e.g., 90d default, 1y segmented, 18m legal-hold) and how keys/identifiers are mapped to customer tenants.
- An export/playbook example: commands or steps, included fields (headers, request id, model version, KV cache indicators), and expected delivery artifacts (s3 manifest, CSV/JSON, checksums).

We have a tight audit timeline (SIG window closes 2027-09-20). Please let me know what you can provide by EOD Tuesday 9/7. If helpful, cc your engineering contact.

—Alex Burns
Head of Security Engineering
MedForge Labs
alex.burns@medforge.com

2) Will MedForge accept exported artifacts delivered to an S3 bucket you control under an encrypted transfer, or do you require Redwood-managed artifact escrow?

We’ll aim to send a draft package by EOD Tuesday (9/7).

Hi team — attaching the working artifacts: medforge_retention_matrix.xlsx and forensics_collection_playbook_v1.pdf (attachments). Below is a short, technical summary that addresses Alex’s bullets.

1) Approval criteria for retention exceptions- Triggering events: legal hold request, active incident response with P1/confirmed compromise, or regulator subpoena.- Required evidence: customer request + signed MA (email thread or contract amendment) + IR ticket with incident summary.- Approvers: Compliance lead (Marissa) + Infra on-call lead (Grace) for initial approval; Legal signs off for subpoenas. Approvals are logged in our ticketing system (Jira SUP-XXXXX).

2) Retention buckets we support- default_request_logs: 90d (standard for hosted tenants)- segmented_tenant_bucket: configurable up to 365d (1 year) for filtered tenants/paths — stored in a separate S3 prefix with lifecycle tags- legal_hold_bucket: up to 18 months (subscription to paid Escrow/Private retention add-on)

Mapping: customer tenant_id -> S3 prefix + retention tag. We surface tenant_id mapping in the Redwood Console for the account owner and in encrypted manifests.

3) Export/playbook (summary) — see attached PDF for full steps; excerpt below:
- Preconditions: signed exception + ticket with tenant_id + time range + reason.
- Collection command (example):
  • run-export --tenant=mf-tenant-123 --start=2026-03-01T00:00:00Z --end=2026-03-31T23:59:59Z --include=meta,headers,request_id,model_id --format=jsonl --dest=s3://redwood-exports/medforge/mf-tenant-123/
- Output artifacts: JSONL files (request-level), s3-export-manifest.txt (line-delimited filenames + checksums), export-metadata.json (exporter version, hash algorithm, row-count).
- Integrity: SHA256 checksums in manifest, server-side encryption AES-256, and an optional PGP envelope if customer requests.
- Timeline: typical export for 30–90 day ranges completes within 24–72 hours depending on tokens scanned and configured batch concurrency.

Attached is also a small sample manifest (s3-export-manifest.txt) and a one-page evidence checklist for SIG reviewers. Marissa — see the approval matrix in the spreadsheet; I flagged the legal_hold path as an add-on item that requires procurement commitment.

On approvals and logging: all exception approvals create a Jira SUP- entry and a console change record (immutable audit entry with approver id). We retain that audit entry per our policy.

Happy to convert any parts of the playbook into runnable scripts if MedForge wants — that would speed exports.

—Grace O’Connor
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
